title: Naturality of homotopy-colimit maps in the value diagram
statement:
Use the model-category, universe, homotopy-colimit and canonical reindexing conventions of [lem-coef-hocolim-reindexing-zigzags]. Let $\mathcal M$ be a combinatorial model category, let $K$ and $J$ be small ordinary categories, and let $g:J\to K$ be a functor. For diagrams $F,G:K\to\mathcal M$ and an objectwise weak-equivalence natural transformation $\eta:F\to G$, choose the functorial projective cofibrant replacements used to define $\operatorname{hocolim}$ and let $H_K(\eta):\operatorname{hocolim}_K F\to\operatorname{hocolim}_K G$ be the induced map. The canonical reindexing comparisons satisfy
$$H_K(\eta)\,g_*^F=g_*^G\,H_J(\eta g),$$
in the homotopy category. If $\eta g$ is the identity transformation, this reduces to $H_K(\eta)g_*^F=g_*^G$.

source.place: Dugger, Combinatorial Model Categories Have Presentations, Appendix A.2 and Remark A.3(i)-(iv), printed pp. 197-198; agent-extracted value-diagram naturality of the canonical comparison, via projective replacement and the localized colimit universal property. No Stacks tag states this model-category assertion. Read online; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: For each small indexing category $I$, [lem-coef-model-colimit-localization-comparison] supplies the projective diagram model structure with objectwise weak equivalences and the localized colimit cocone associated to a projectively cofibrant replacement. Choose the stipulated functorial replacements $Q_I$. Functoriality gives a map $Q_K(\eta):Q_KF\to Q_KG$, and applying the ordinary colimit gives $H_K(\eta)=\operatorname{colim}_K Q_K(\eta)$; its localized class is the induced map of homotopy colimits.

source.place: Appendix A.2 and Remark A.3(i), printed pp.197-198; functorial projective replacement and induced homotopy-colimit map.

proof.text: Let (lambda_F:q(Fg)	o qH_J(Fg)) and (lambda_G:q(Gg)	o qH_J(Gg)) denote the localized colimit cocones supplied by [lem-coef-model-colimit-localization-comparison], and let the restricted (K)-cocones define (g_*^F) and (g_*^G) as in [lem-coef-hocolim-reindexing-zigzags]. Naturality of the replacement augmentations gives, object by object, commuting squares between the (F)- and (G)-cocone legs; after localization these say that (H_K(eta)g_*^F) and (g_*^G H_J(eta g)) induce the same cocone (q(Fg)	o qH_K(G)). This argument does not identify (Q_J(Fg)) with the restriction of (Q_KF); it uses only the localized cocone universal property. The universal property therefore identifies the two maps, yielding (H_K(eta),g_*^F=g_*^G,H_J(eta g)) in the homotopy category.

source.place: Appendix A.2 and Remark A.3(ii)-(iii), printed pp.197-198; naturality of canonical reindexing comparisons in the value diagram.

proof.text: If $\eta g$ is the identity transformation, functoriality of the chosen replacement gives $Q_J(\eta g)=1$, hence $H_J(\eta g)=1$ in the homotopy category. Substituting this identity into the square of Step 2 gives $H_K(\eta)g_*^F=g_*^G$.

source.place: Appendix A.2 and Remark A.3(i)-(iii), printed pp.197-198; identity specialization.

proof_origin.place: Proof paragraph 2: naturality of the canonical reindexing comparison in the value diagram; Dugger Appendix A.2 and Remark A.3(i)-(iii).
